subject.title: [Feature]: 内置健壮性机制：Watchdog、全局错误处理、自动恢复

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in Gateway watchdog and recovery ladder, and which recovery actions should be default, opt-in, or out of scope?
rationale: The request crosses process supervision, config schema, doctor repair, degraded startup, notifications, and security-sensitive operator authority, so source inspection cannot choose permanent product semantics safely.

options.title: Design opt-in core recovery
options.body: Keep the umbrella open while maintainers define a narrow opt-in recovery policy and split implementation into smaller owned follow-ups.

options.title: Split into narrower trackers
options.body: Replace the broad item with separate canonical issues for process watchdog, health schema, error policy, degraded startup, and notifications.

options.title: Reject core ownership
options.body: Close the request as out of core scope and document supervisor, plugin, or operator-owned recovery patterns instead.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in core recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the umbrella open while maintainers define a narrow opt-in recovery policy and split implementation into smaller owned follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: The requested global error policy and Gateway recovery semantics overlap Peter Steinberger's unhandled-rejection and watchdog-adjacent history.
